answer: Latency debt ledger: each identity accrues a persistent score of unanswered peer requests. Past a ridge threshold, its messages route through a slower queue, cutting throughput. Attackers see per-identity latency compound linearly with count, so operating many identities costs proportionally more wall-clock time than one. A gale of duplicates stalls itself. Scores decay only via sustained real replies, priced in opal-grade compute per verified response.
